main_body: Half-timbered house with a large red tile hip/gable roof, plaster-and-timber front walls, a door and a window, and a front gable wing with its own door
top_band: Tile roof slopes in orange to red-brown with light tile highlights, about rows 1-26 above the left wall (the roof is the top surface, seen from above)
evidence: Reading down the left wall column: tile roof slopes fill roughly rows 1-26 (several consecutive rows with per-tile highlights). A dark eave row at about rows 26-27 sits on top of the timber frame, then the plaster front face (about rows 28-44) with timber posts and braces. The gable wing repeats this: roof slope, then a triangular gable wall, then a lower wall with a door. The roof slopes are clearly visible surfaces, and the front wall sits under a dark eave line. Doors and windows are framed with dark inner edges. This matches the Beodeul reference buildings.

style.evidence: The roof has per-tile scallops and highlights with 5-6 steps from cream-yellow through orange to maroon. Outlines are dark brown or maroon next to the wood and tiles, not black. The plaster carries speckle dots, the timber has grain, and the brick chimney is shaded brick by brick. It is as rich as the reference houses, with no large flat fills.
